subtype: Approach: only avoids bad outcomes and never defines a positive goal [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday: Raghav wrote his final-year plan as a list of things not to do: don't take a risky elective, don't join a busy club, don't apply anywhere he might not get in, don't pay for courses he might not finish. Preeti read it over his shoulder and said it looked safe.

Thursday: Raghav showed the plan to a senior and noticed that every line said what to avoid. No line said what he wanted. 'What are you aiming at?' asked Preeti. He couldn't say.

Following Monday: Raghav put down his pen. He had a plan that couldn't fail, and it also led nowhere. His week had been full of careful non-choices, and he still had no idea what he wanted to be doing in a year.

qa.q: What did every line of Raghav's plan say?
qa.a: Every line said what to avoid.

qa.q: How did Raghav feel when Preeti asked what he was aiming at?
qa.a: Raghav felt stuck and empty, since he couldn't answer and saw the plan pointed nowhere.

qa.q: What other step could Raghav take to build a real direction?
qa.a: Raghav could write down one thing he wants to be doing in a year and choose a small step toward it each month, keeping the avoid list as a side note.

qa.q: How might Preeti have seen the plan?
qa.a: Preeti probably saw a safe but empty plan, which is why Preeti said it looked safe and asked what Raghav was aiming at.

grounding: Shows a student who avoids every mistake he can think of, ending with a safe, empty plan and no positive goal.
